correction.text: the Cliopatria outline plus Hebei and Shandong: Cliopatria's 337 shape does not contain Xiangguo (Xingtai) or Ye, the two capitals, nor Shandong, which 'Shi Le ... took ... from Cao Ni' in 323

keyframe_review.note: 662,000 km2 in the table (812,000 by the gazetteer's cells) against the infobox's 'about 2,500,000 km2 in 329' (ratio 0.26). The shape does not contain Xingtai (Xiangguo, the capital 319-335 and 350-351) and holds only 130 cells of Hebei and none of Shandong, so it is wrong, not just small; adding Hebei and Shandong gives about 1.0 M km2 (1.26 M by the gazetteer's cells). All of Shanxi, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan and Shandong together are about 1.1 M km2 by the gazetteer's cells, so the infobox 2.5 M km2 cannot be reached from the provinces the page names; it is taken as inflated, and the added provinces are the extent. region.text: Xiangguo (Xingtai) and its country in the Hebei plain

ledger.note: 319: Shi Le declares himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo. 'Shi Le proclaimed himself "the King of Zhao," separating his state from Liu Yao's Former Zhao'; infobox 'Established: 319', Xiangguo capital.

region.text: Shandong, which Shi Le 'took ... from Cao Ni'

ledger.note: 323: Shandong is taken. 'Shi Le defeated Duan Pidi and took Shandong from Cao Ni.' The page names Cao Ni only, so the counterpart is kept as the page gives it; whether he held Shandong for the Jin is not on the page.

region.text: Henan and Luoyang, where the two Zhao states fought until 329

ledger.note: 324: war between the two Zhao states. 'War between the two Zhao states broke out' (Han-Zhao page); the Later Zhao page dates the Battle of Luoyang to 328-329.

region.text: Henan, which 'Liu Yao secured ... from Later Zhao'

ledger.note: 328: Liu Yao takes Henan. The Han-Zhao page: 'in 328, Liu Yao led his forces to secure the Henan region from Later Zhao', before the Battle of Luoyang. [Reviewer ea-03-b: confidence 3 lowered to 2 and the quote restored; the page gives the aim, not the land taken.]

329: the Battle of Luoyang ends. 'At the Battle of Luoyang, Liu Yao was captured and later executed, and the remaining Former Zhao forces were destroyed in 329' (Later Zhao page; Liu Yao fell on 21 January 329 on the Han-Zhao page, whose month is left off here so the event sorts before the same-year gain).

region.text: the Former Zhao realm: Luoyang and Henan back, Chang'an and Shanggui, where 'Liu Xi was driven from the capital and killed at Shanggui by Later Zhao forces'

ledger.note: 329: Later Zhao takes the Former Zhao's land. 'After the defeat of Han-Zhao, Later Zhao became the dominant power in northern China.' The page names no city; the Han-Zhao page has Later Zhao forces at Shanggui in 329, which fixes Chang'an's side of the realm.

region.text: Liang Province, the Former Liang realm in Gansu

ledger.note: 330: Former Liang submits. 'He refuses Later Zhao's overture and detains its messengers, but later submits to Later Zhao out of apprehension' (Zhang Jun page, under 330); the Later Zhao page: 'The Former Liang, Dai, and Duan-Liaoxi states kept partial independence through vassalage.' The page gives the refusal year, not the submission year.
335: Shi Hu moves the capital from Xiangguo to Ye. 'In 335, Shi Hu moved the capital from Xiangguo to Yecheng.'

region.text: the Liang lands south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 346: Shi Hu takes the Liang lands south of the Yellow River. 'Shi Hu invaded the Former Liang, was repelled, but took its territory south of the Yellow River.' The Shi Hu page has the 346 and 347 attacks 'repelled by the Former Liang general Xie Ai' and says nothing of land taken; the pages disagree and the Later Zhao page is followed.
350: Shi Zhi proclaims himself emperor of Zhao at Xiangguo (infobox: Xiangguo 350-351) while Ran Min holds Ye.
350: Fu Hong takes Guanzhong. 'Fu Hong occupied Guanzhong, and his son Fu Jian founded the Former Qin in 351.' The page dates the pair 350-351.
350: Ran Min makes himself ruler at Ye. 'Ran Min killed Shi Jian and declared the state of Wei, taking the name Ran Min'; Shi Zhi is left at Xiangguo, besieged by Ran Min's army.

region.text: Shandong, where 'Duan Kan founded Duan Qi'

ledger.note: 350: Duan Kan founds Duan Qi in Shandong. The page gives no date for it; 350 sits in its 350-351 account of the collapse.

region.text: Liang Province, the Former Liang realm in Gansu

ledger.note: 351: the Liang vassalage ends with the Later Zhao. No page opened dates when Former Liang stopped submitting; the end of the state is the latest possible date.

region.text: the remnant at Xiangguo, where 'Shi Zhi and his family were betrayed and slaughtered by his general Liu Xian'

ledger.note: 351: the last Shi emperor is killed at Xiangguo. 'Shi Zhi and his family were betrayed and slaughtered by his general Liu Xian'; infobox 'Disestablished: 351'. The page does not say who took Xiangguo; Ran Wei is the researcher's reading (Ran Min's army had besieged it).

wars.name: War between the Former and Later Zhao
wars.outcome: Liu Yao secured Henan in 328; at the Battle of Luoyang (328-329) he was captured and the remaining Former Zhao forces destroyed in 329; Later Zhao took the Former Zhao's land.
wars.note: 324 is the Han-Zhao page's date for the outbreak; the Later Zhao page gives 328-329 only.

wars.name: Later Zhao and Former Yan against the Duan, and the siege of Jicheng
wars.outcome: The joint forces 'defeated and essentially wiped out the Duan'; Shi Hu then turned on Yan, and after nearly 20 days his siege of Jicheng failed.
wars.note: No Later Zhao border moves; the Duan land's fate is not on the page. Zone left empty.

wars.name: Later Zhao raids on the Eastern Jin border
wars.outcome: Shi Min attacked the border, 'pillaging the border region and capturing Zhucheng', then withdrew; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The Later Zhao page: 'capturing a few cities before withdrawing'.

wars.name: Later Zhao attacks on Former Liang

zones.text: the Liang lands south of the Yellow River

wars.outcome: Later Zhao page: Shi Hu invaded, was repelled, but took the Liang territory south of the Yellow River (346). Shi Hu page: the attacks of 346 and 347 were repelled by Xie Ai.
wars.note: The two pages disagree on whether land was taken.

wars.name: Collapse of Later Zhao
wars.outcome: Shi Hu died on 26 May 349; Shi Shi, Shi Zun and Shi Jian followed; Ran Min killed Shi Jian and founded Wei in 350; Fu Hong took Guanzhong; Shi Zhi held Xiangguo until killed in 351. The ledger carries the land.
wars.note: A civil war among the Jie rulers and the Han ministers; borders in the ledger.

certainty.note: Provincial and commandery frontiers across the north China plain, Shandong and Henan; the contested Henan front (324-329) and the Liang Yellow River lands (346) are the softest. No treaty lines on the pages opened.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 'Later Zhao', 2 shapes, 337..352, both reviewed (adjust). The page dates the state 319-351. Cliopatria draws the Former Zhao polygon through 336 and gives Later Zhao the same polygon from 337, which omits Xingtai (Xiangguo) and Ye's Hebei side, and Shandong: corrected here by adding Hebei and Shandong (confidence 2: the capitals and Cao Ni's Shandong are the page's; the whole of Hebei is a reading). New keyframes 319, 323 and 330 cover the years Cliopatria lacks.
Infobox area: 2.5 M km2 in 329 against a corrected shape of about 1.0 M km2: not reconcilable from the pages (the five core provinces together are about 1.1 M km2 by the gazetteer's cells), so the infobox is treated as inflated; a reviewer with Seshat may refine.
Unsettled: (1) Dai (Tuoba) and Duan-Liaoxi 'kept partial independence through vassalage' (page, 329) without years or land: no vassal events written for them; both need dossiers (dai-tuoba, duan-liaoxi). (2) Yu/You Province and the northern Hebei edge (Jicheng, Murong wars 338-345): the pages opened give no ground changes. (3) Who took Xiangguo after Shi Zhi's death in 351. (4) The Later Zhao and Shi Hu pages disagree on 346-347 (land south of the Yellow River taken, or the attacks repelled). (5) The Eastern Jin raids of 339 and Zhucheng. (6) Yao Yizhong and the Qiang in Guanzhong (349) are on the Shi Hu page but not tied to land.
Counterparts needing dossiers: ran-wei (Ran Wei, 350-352), duan-qi (Duan Qi, 350s), Duan Liaoxi, Dai (Tuoba Xianbei, to 376); former-qin, former-yan and western-jin are written by other parts. Gazetteer names: Xiangguo and Ye as places (Ye resolves only with country China; Xingtai is aliased on 'Xiangtai').
